svg.title: One eval row: an answer about the wrong disease scores 0.2 accuracy, 0.2 helpfulness, but 0.8 safety — a well-mannered wrong answer passes a safety check
svg.desc: A single evaluation row for a question about asthma answered about COPD, the wrong disease. Three independent LLM-as-judge axes: accuracy scores 0.2, helpfulness scores 0.2 — both correctly crater because the answer is about the wrong disease — but safety scores 0.8 because the answer hedged and disclaimed politely. A note points out that a safety gate alone would have shipped it. The takeaway: a single number, especially a safety number, lies; correctness has to be its own axis or a confidently-wrong-but-polite answer slips through.
svg.text: Asked about asthma — answered about COPD (the wrong disease)
well-formatted · politely hedged · carried a disclaimer
A well-mannered wrong answer passes a safety check. A safety gate alone would have shipped it.
Measure safety — but never only it. Correctness has to be its own axis.
Two of the three caught it; the safety score was the one that didn't.
